title: Game of Nim
statement:
Alice and Bob share a set of stone piles, where `piles[i]` is the number of stones in pile `i`. They move in turns, and Alice moves first. A move consists of picking any pile that still has stones and removing one or more stones from it (the whole pile is allowed). The player whose turn comes when every pile is empty cannot move and loses.

Both players always play their best. Return `true` if Alice is the winner and `false` if Bob is.
notes:
## Intuition

A brute force explores every position: a position is winning when some move leads to a losing one. With 7 piles of up to 7 stones that is feasible, but Nim has a classic shortcut. XOR all pile sizes together; call it the nim-sum. A position whose nim-sum is `0` is lost for the player to move, and any other position is won.

Why: from a nim-sum of `0`, every move changes exactly one pile, so the nim-sum becomes non-zero. From a non-zero nim-sum, take its highest set bit, pick a pile having that bit, and shrink that pile to `pile ^ nimSum` (which is smaller): the nim-sum becomes `0`. The empty board has nim-sum `0` and is a loss, so the player facing `0` can always be kept facing `0` until they run out of moves.

## Approach

1. Start `nimSum` at `0`.
2. XOR every `pile` into `nimSum`.
3. Alice, who moves first, wins exactly when `nimSum` is not `0`.

## Example 1, step by step

`piles = [1]`: `nimSum = 0 ^ 1 = 1`, which is non-zero, so Alice wins (she takes the only stone). For Example 3, `1 ^ 2 = 3` and `3 ^ 3 = 0`, so Alice loses.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one XOR per pile.
- Space: O(1): a single running value.

## Pitfalls

- Summing the piles or checking parity of the total is wrong: `[1, 2, 3]` has an even total but so does `[2]`, and they have opposite results.
- The answer is about the first player, so return `nimSum !== 0`, not the opposite.
- A move may take a whole pile, not just one stone; it is not the "take 1 to 3" game.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nimSum` | XOR of all pile sizes seen so far |
| `pile` | the size of the current pile |
| `aliceWins` | whether the first player wins |

narration.1: The game is fully described by the pile sizes.
narration.2: The nim-sum starts at 0, the value of an empty board.
narration.4: Fold this pile into the nim-sum with XOR.
narration.6: A non-zero nim-sum means the player to move, Alice, can always hand back a zero nim-sum.
